## First a review of Markdown

As a reminder, we can make text **bold** with two stars, or *italics* with one star.

## Next I'll load my libraries so I can do stuff with ggplot2
```{r}
#| warnings: false
library("ggplot2")

# TODO: load file

```

## Now I'll include a ggplot2 graph
Note: Each plot should be it's own code block

```{r}
# scatter plot with x and y
ggplot(data = midwest) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = percollege, y = percadultpoverty))

```

```{r}
# histogram
ggplot(data = midwest) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(x = poptotal), 
    binwidth = 2000
  )
```




```{r}
ggplot(data = midwest) +
  geom_point(
    mapping = aes(
      x = percollege, 
      y = percadultpoverty,
      color = state)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Percent College Educated versus Poverty Rates", # plot title
    x = "Percentage of College Educated Adults", # x-axis label
    y = "Percentage of Adults Living in Poverty", # y-axis label
    color = "State" # Legend label for the "color" property
  )

```

## code in paragraphs
Reminder on how to calculate values and put them in paragraphs
```{r}
num_counties = nrow(midwest)
```

There were `r num_counties` counties in our dataset.
